messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: RStan's DESCRIPTION and LICENSE
parts:
I am about to make it possible to install RStan using 
install.packages('rstan', repos='http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R')
so that Andrew could easily install RStan. 
I just revised the DESCRIPTION and LICENSE of rstan (under STAN_HOME/stan/rstan/rstan). 
Please take a look and revise them if needed as I was not serious enough about LICENSE and authorship
before. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: RStan's DESCRIPTION and LICENSE
parts:
On Monday, August 6, 2012 10:41:11 PM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
I just revised the DESCRIPTION and LICENSE of rstan (under STAN_HOME/stan/rstan/rstan). 
Please take a look and revise them if needed as I was not serious enough about LICENSE and authorship
before.

Is it correct that RStan does not modify any of the code under rstan/inst/include ? If so, then I think the DESCRIPTION can say

License: GPL (>= 3)

and then add a

LicenseNote: RStan includes unmodified copies of X, Y, Z all of which are available at x, y, z under open-source licenses that are compatible with version 3 of the GPL.

That is more or less what RcppEigen does. Being able to put 

License: GPL (>= 3)

rather than

License: FILE

is good because some companies grep the DESCRIPTION of all package to avoid installing / using any GPL code and others grep the DESCRIPTION to only use FLOSS.

In general, RStan should follow the FSF's guidelines (although a lot of packages don't)

https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-howto.html

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan's DESCRIPTION and LICENSE
parts:
I think we should do exactly what Ben suggests.

If RStan does modify any of the code in rstan/inst/include, we should
rearrange things so that it doesn't.

We should only be redistributing a part of Boost, and nothing
from Eigen or Google Test. Eigen we'll get through RCppEigen and
Google Code we don't need at all.

I'm going to remove all unsupported Eigen packages from the
C++ Stan repository other than FFT unless anyone objects.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan's DESCRIPTION and LICENSE
parts:
On Friday, August 10, 2012 2:31:38 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I'm going to remove all unsupported Eigen packages from the
C++ Stan repository other than FFT unless anyone objects.

I am not objecting, but I can't see why having them around in the repository would cause a problem if Stan does not (currently) utilize them. I could see the Kronecker, MatrixFunctions, and MoreVectorization modules being useful to somebody, although such a somebody is presumably more than capable of putting those modules back in. The optimization-related ones are also pretty good, although I guess Stan is going to do its own soon.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan's DESCRIPTION and LICENSE
parts:
On 8/10/12 2:52 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Friday, August 10, 2012 2:31:38 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
> I'm going to remove all unsupported Eigen packages from the
> C++ Stan repository other than FFT unless anyone objects.
>
>
> I am not objecting, but I can't see why having them around in the repository would cause a problem if Stan does not
> (currently) utilize them.

There are two problems:

1. It produces more code for false hits when
searching. For instance, I don't want anyone
to confuse the Eigen auto-dif for what we're doing
for auto-dif, and

2. It's just more code to download, though given how much
we have, I doubt it'll be noticeable.

> I could see the Kronecker, MatrixFunctions, and MoreVectorization modules being useful to
> somebody, although such a somebody is presumably more than capable of putting those modules back in. The
> optimization-related ones are also pretty good, although I guess Stan is going to do its own soon.

Right. I don't know when we'll get to optimization.
It would be pretty easy. But then it'd also make sense
to just use Stan's model classes and then use someone else's
optimization package.

Also, I wish they'd just support these or get rid of them.
Having the tag "unsupported" in the file path makes me very
nervous. So I'd rather not use these things unless it's
absolutely necessary. The use of unsupported/Eigen/FFT was a tradeoff
between licensing issues and fear of using unsupported modules.
For example, Eigen's FFT seems unlikely to be upgraded with
new versions of KissFFT, of which there have been several since
Eigen's incorporation of KissFFT.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan's DESCRIPTION and LICENSE
parts:
On Friday, August 10, 2012 3:01:38 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Also, I wish they'd just support these or get rid of them.
Having the tag "unsupported" in the file path makes me very
nervous.  So I'd rather not use these things unless it's
absolutely necessary.

Some unsupported modules are more supported than others. But Eigen only has a few main developers and a ton of users, so they don't want to promise things they can't deliver. But if there were a problem with something in unsupported/ , someone would presumably be willing to talk about it on the list and try to fix it if it didn't require rewriting something in the main part of Eigen. For FFT, it was probably worth it.

Ben
